title: InferCT: An Efficient and Generalizable Framework to Enable 3D Machine Learning for Computed Tomography
problem: 3D deep learning models for CT inference require large GPU memory, limiting practical deployment. Existing approaches struggle with dataset size variability and imaging task diversity.
motivation: 3D models outperform 2D approaches for CT analysis but are impractical at inference due to memory constraints. Need a general framework independent of dataset size and task.
method: InferCT partitions CT volumes into cubic sub-volumes fitting GPU memory, distributing across multiple GPUs. Adds vendor-agnostic optimizations: lock-free shared memory data structure, pipeline execution to hide prefetching/post-processing latency, and parallel data loader.
key_novelty: Vendor-agnostic framework combining volume partitioning with lock-free synchronization and pipelined execution for efficient 3D CT inference.
contributions: 1.97x speedup over baseline for 1024³ datasets (AMD MI300X and NVIDIA H100)
Strong scaling: 89.25% efficiency (1-4 GPUs, single NUMA node)
75.75% efficiency scaling across NUMA nodes (1-8 GPUs)
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Evaluation limited to image denoising task. Generalization to other medical imaging modalities not addressed.
primary_theme: Efficient 3D medical imaging inference on GPUs
